entry.dc:title: Geodynamic phenomena induced by the opencast mining activity at Belchatow.
entry.dc:creator: Wysokinski L.
entry.prism:publicationName: Proc 5th International Association of Engineering Geology Congress Buenos Aires 1986 Vol 1 Balkema
entry.dc:description: The seismic activity phenomenon induced by the mining works at the Belchatow open-pit mine of depth down to 200 m is described. The phenomenon mechanism was discussed and the forecasted values of tremors calculated on the basis of the simplified seismic hazard method are presented. -from Author

entry.dc:title: OPENCAST MINING OF PREVIOUSLY UNDERGROUND-MINED COAL SEAMS.
entry.dc:creator: Clough W.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of the South African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: The presence of bord-and-pillar workings within the No. 2 seam of the Witbank Coalfield of South Africa requires that different methods of mining should be considered, depending on the location of the workings. The paper describes some basic methods of underground mining the seam.

entry.dc:title: HOMOGENIZATION SYSTEM FOR RUN-OF-MINE COAL AT THE EKIBASTUZ COAL FIELD.
entry.dc:creator: Krueckemeier R.
entry.dc:description: This paper discusses one of the largest opencast mining operations for the excavation of bituminous coal, the Ekibastuz field in Kasachstan, USSR. Background for this large-scale stockyard order was PWH's leading position and high technology standard in erecting high-capacity terminals and stockyards as well as the high standard in the field of opencast mining technology. Four homogenization systems, each with a storage capacity of 100,000 t and a stockpiling capacity of 6000 t/h, are interlinked between the mining operation and the shipment of the coal. The reclaiming capacity per system and reclaimer amounts to 4000 t/h. The systems are run in three operating shifts at approx. 6000 working hours per year.

entry.dc:title: OPENCAST MINING AND THE ENVIRONMENT.
entry.dc:creator: Tomlinson J.D.
entry.dc:description: This article discusses the work of the Opencast Executive of the NCB with reference to noise control, noise measurement, blasting, control of ground vibrations, water pollution, dust problems and land reclamation.

entry.dc:title: ASPECTS OF ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT FOR OPEN PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Streit E.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: Raw materials for basic industry and power generating plants are excavated in opencast mines by two different mining methods: continuous mining, employing bucket wheel excavators; and discontinuous mining (strip mining), employing draglines and shovels. Depending upon the geological structure of the mine a combination of both methods can also be used. The main equipment-groups for opencast mining are: bucket wheel excavator, conveyor system, tripper car and spreader. Since all these equipment are driven by electric motors, an extensive range of power equipment is necessary.

entry.dc:title: MODERN OPEN-PIT MINING TECHNOLOGY.
entry.dc:creator: Ringleff H.
entry.dc:description: This paper describes two types of opencast mining technologies, which have been developed for more efficiency and reliability with regard to continuous bulk material handling. The conceptual design of a phosphate mining system is a combination of continuous bucket wheel operation, dragline strip mining, reclaiming by means of bucketwheel, and pumping the phosphate slurry in pipelines. Shiftable and mobile crushing units are special opencast systems used for hard rock formations.

entry.dc:title: Opencast mining and the environment
entry.dc:creator: Tomlinson J.

entry.dc:title: Seismic spectroscopy in fracture characterization.
entry.dc:creator: Young R.P.
entry.dc:description: As part of a research project to assess fracturing in rock masses on opencast coal sites, empirical correlations are being developed which relate fracture characteristics to the attenuation of seismic signals. An experimental programme into the design of efficient blasting/fragmentation systems in opencast mining is outlined. The results show that the fragmentation efficiency of a mine blast can be quantified in terms of 3-D seismic attenuation spectra and polar anisotropy diagrams. A data case study is given to highlight the scope of the data collected and the type of multivariate statistical analysis methods used.-from Authors

entry.dc:title: Authorisation procedures for opencast mining.
entry.dc:creator: Peart J.D.
entry.dc:description: A review of the change in planning law which transfers development control powers over opencast mining to mineral planning authorities. Three perspectives are forwarded: 1) the planning authorities are detrimentally affected by inadequate staffing, and the lack of any national policy for either energy or opencast coal; 2) the National Coal Board are concerned that the new procedures are too slow, and 3) the environmental lobby has been outmanoeuvred and should press for the more comprehensive legislation available in the USA.-A.Gilg

entry.dc:title: COAL EXPORT POTENTIAL FROM INDIA'S EAST COAST.
entry.dc:creator: Bordia S.
entry.dc:description: On April 1, 1984, India had surplus coal stocks of about 20 mt stored near coal mines and this surplus is likely to increase as newer and bigger opencast mining projects are commissioned. India can therefore plan to export 10 mt of steam coal from coal regions near the eastern sea coast. This paper presents a brief outline of the export plan, involving coal basins to be developed, the mining system to be employed, the transportation system from coal mines to ports, port facilities to be developed, capital investment required and expected earnings from the coal exports.

entry.dc:title: QUALITY PROFILE OF A BLAST.
entry.dc:creator: Murari K.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of the Institution of Engineers India Mining Engineering Division
entry.dc:description: Mechanization is necessary for a higher output in opencast mining. To produce several thousand tons of ores a day of a mine-run, the bench height must be increased. Drilling patterns are chosen in such a manner that blasting is done either weekly or fortnightly. In this paper a method of predicting the quality of the broken rock mass is described and its application in openpit mines indicated.

entry.dc:title: Problems of Flue Gas Gypsum Disposal as Exemplified by the Rhenish Lignite District.
entry.dc:creator: Bloss W.
entry.dc:description: As can be judged at present, it does not seem possible for the gypsum and cement industries to absorb the expected quantities of flue gas gypsum arising from coal-fired and lignite-fired power stations. Based on the need to develop new applications for these quantities, a disposal scheme for lignite-fired plants is proposed which consists of using the gypsum in combination with lignite ash as a filling material in opencast mining.

entry.dc:title: A strategy for nature conservation.
entry.dc:description: Describes the wildlife resources of Wigan, Lancashire, and the key wildlife sites. The threats and pressures are outlined, ranging from opencast mining to intensive recreation use. Then presents the strategy, which is divided into 1) protection and enhancement of existing interest - policies on waste tipping, land reclamation and effective management; 2) creation of wildlife areas - ecological planting, land reclamation and urban nature parks; 3) environmental awareness - wildlife surveys and interpretation.-R.Land

entry.dc:title: (Pursuing the phenomena associated with opencast mining by means of earth- remote sensing).
entry.dc:creator: Plachy S.
entry.dc:description: Investigates mining characteristics, using multispectral and multitemporal methods. The area investigated was 200 km<sup>2</sup> of brown coal mining round Teplice (Teplitz). It uses a AFA-39-M Camera and MSP-4 interpretation. Orthophotographs were used at 3 dates eleven years apart. The 'digikart' system was used to quantify the area devastated. Four classes of objects were chosen. Methods of expressing the results are compared and their reliability evaluated. -D.J.Davis

entry.dc:title: DUMPTRUCKS FOR QUARRYING AND OPENCAST MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: The article covers articulated trucks, safety factors, noise reduction, tire care, rolling resistance, technical innovations, truck productivity and the market situation in the UK.

entry.dc:title: PLANT AND EQUIPMENT USED IN OPENCAST MINING AND ASSOCIATED ACTIVITIES.
entry.dc:creator: Brook C.
entry.dc:description: The NCB Opencast Executive produces low-ash high-quality coal for industrial markets. Opencast sites vary in workable reserves from a few thousand tonnes up to several million tonnes. A discussion is given on the following: the three basic working methods (the motor scraper, the dragline, and the face shovel/dump truck); a description of practices in site working; environmental considerations (blasting, noise, dust, and water pollution); disposal points for the mined coal; and future prospects.

entry.dc:title: AIR PHOTOGRAPHS FOR INVESTIGATING NATURAL CHANGES, PAST USE AND PRESENT CONDITION OF ENGINEERING SITES.
entry.dc:creator: Dumbleton M.
entry.prism:publicationName: TRRL Laboratory Report Transport and Road Research Laboratory Great Britain
entry.dc:description: Air photographs can play an important part in the investigation of engineering sites because they provide an overall view which can reveal surface features, ground conditions, and evidence of past use and natural changes which may be of importance in site development. Historical series of available air photographs can often allow the history of past use and natural change to be followed in detail over the last 35 years or more. The Report reviews the availability of air photographs and gives details of some 20 major sources and collections for the UK. The interpretation of air photographs is discussed, and illustrated by two case studies in which historical series of available photographs allowed the construction and demolition of brick works, the excavation and filling of clay pits, and the progress of opencast mining and restoration to be followed in detail. In addition, examples are given of the successful use of air photographs in the investigation of a wide range of engineering problems.

entry.dc:title: The application of soil survey data in opencast coal sites in Scotland
entry.dc:creator: Gauld J.H.
entry.dc:description: A commitment by the National Coal Board Opencast Executive to restore opencast coal areas to agricultural use as efficiently as possible recognizes the need for continual improvement in techniques. The Department of Agriculture and Fisheries for Scotland, as agents to the National Coal Board Opencast Executive, share a similar objective. Both organizations appreciate the need for a comprehensive soil survey, but experience has shown that general-purpose maps and reports are not always adequate for use in opencast mining operations. A soil survey of a proposed site at Keirsbeath is described and, on the basis of results from the use of improved survey methodology, and computer techniques to analyse the data, interpretative maps have been produced. The procedures, together with an examination of soil quantities available for restoration, and of critical moisture levels in soil stripping, are an improvement with significance for the planning and development work stage. A scheme of soil operations has been presented and the relevance of soil data to the forthcoming restoration and rehabilitation stages is discussed. © 1983.

entry.dc:title: Water and soil guideline for mining.
entry.dc:creator: Lawrence J.
entry.dc:description: Covers mining of unconsolidated alluvial and coastal sediments and offshore mineral and petroleum deposits; rock quarry mining, non-metallic opencast mining and underground and opencast hardrock metallic and coal mining. The guideline is divided into four sections set in the context of management planning. These are: 1) a description of the statutes which cover prospecting and mining; 2) the potential impacts on water and soil resources; 3) the minimisation or avoidance of these impacts; and 4) mining operations which require special attention from a water and soil viewpoint.-from Editors

entry.dc:title: Morphogenetic approach to man-made landforms due to opencast mining of porcelain clays and silica sands, around Seto City, Aichi Prefecture, central Japan.
entry.dc:creator: Moriyama A.
entry.dc:description: Landforms of mining fields are generally characterized by disordered distribution of large mining hollows such as honeycombs. Each hollow consists of steep cliffs, step-like benches, abandoned roads and settling basins in the bottom of hollows. The Mizuno Gravel Bed which is called the 'surface layer' by mine workers is excavated and transported to the abandoned mining fields or the upper part of valleys to make flat or rolling surfaces. New machines such as large bulldozers, power-shovels and loader shovels have greatly exaggerated the landform transformation. Present detailed features such as height and width of bench cliffs, benches and roads of mining fields seem to be provided by the capacity and function of these heavy machines and dump cars. -from English summary

entry.dc:title: SEISMIC REMOTE SENSING OF ROCK MASSES FOR THE OPTIMIZATION OF EXCAVATION EFFICIENCY.
entry.dc:creator: Young R.P.
entry.prism:publicationName: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
entry.dc:description: A seismic remote sensing technique and the associated microprocessor-based instrumentation are described, as part of three phases of a research project into the design of efficient blasting/fragmentation systems in opencast mining. The experimental program outlined involves the remote assessment of rock quality before and after a blast, together with the monitoring of the associated ground vibration and excavation process in order to assess blast fragmentation efficiency. An overview of the experimental program and instrumentation is given together with preliminary results from phase three of the research.

entry.dc:title: DEVELOPMENT TRENDS IN THE CONSTRUCTION OF SPREADERS FOR OPENCAST MINE DUMPS: PART 2. CROSS-PIT-SPREADERS.
entry.dc:creator: Weiss A.
entry.dc:description: Direct haulage of overburden over the shortest distance across the open pit to the mine area where the useful seams were already exploited represents the oldest and most economic method of exposing deposits by application of opencast mining techniques. For increased digging heights, the method of continuous overburden transport by means of conveying bridges was introduced. These systems require an additional travel path at the dumping side and their design needs to be exactly tailored to the geometric dimensions in a specific mine. For exposal of deeper seams in large opencast mines, extensive application of the 'around-the-pit' method is made.

entry.dc:title: OPENCAST MINING - THE CUMBRIAN SCENE.
entry.dc:creator: Mck. Guyan J.
entry.dc:description: Following the explosion in oil prices in 1973 the Plan for Coal 1974 required the Opencast Executive to expand production from around 6/7M tonnes to 15M tonnes. Cumbria's share was approximately 1M tonnes. Subsequent to 1974 six sites have been authorized. These are Low Close Extension, Outgang, Oughterside, Foxhouse, Moresby and Keekle and Pica with production continuing from all but Outgang which is currently undergoing restoration.

entry.dc:title: TOTAL SYSTEM CONCEPT IN PLANNING AND IMPLEMENTATION OF INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT OF IRON ORES, FLUXES & INFRASTRUCTURAL FACILITIES REQUIRED FOR IRON AND STEEL INDUSTRY IN INDIA.
entry.dc:creator: Khuntia G.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: Some aspects of planning the Indian iron and steel industry are reviewed to cover principal raw materials and their conservation; quality control practices; traffic and power requirements; application of computers in opencast mining; provision of adequate capital; corporate organization for planning and monitoring the performance and development of mineral reserve base. It is shown that a time bound program for development and growth of mines producing principal raw materials for iron and steel industry has to be worked out. The main objective should be to supply adequate raw materials with highest productivity utilizing existing capacities and for providing additional capacities in time to produce maximum raw materials with minimum production cost.

entry.dc:title: Analysis of mineral wear processes with particular reference to open-cut mining equipment.
entry.dc:creator: Besser D.
entry.dc:description: Abrasive wear process are marked by high intensities of wear. Such wearing processes can be classified in three large groups, the most complex group being that of 3-body wear in which two solid bodies are moving against each other under the influence of mineral abrasives. Influential factors affecting such processes were analyzed in the laboratory, and the results obtained were confirmed by those obtained for lignite opencast mining equipment. (English abstract)
